subject: Pricing: Acme AI - budget owner & unit economics
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya@acme-ai.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 15:05:00 -0800
Subject: RE: Intro + demo — pricing follow-up and next steps

Hi Maya — great to meet today, thanks for the time. Quick recap and next steps from our side: 

- Token volumes: you mentioned peak inference ~10M tokens/day for the NLU service and average ~3M tokens/day across other pipelines (training/evals are separate). You also noted potential growth to ~20–25M tokens/day within 6–9 months if the roadmap goes well.
- Current budget range: you said Finance is targeting an initial committed spend in the $60k–$120k/month range for inference (flexible depending on commitments/discounting).
- Procurement constraints: you flagged that Procurement + Finance will need a formal quote and that Tom Rivers (Finance) will sign off.

Ask for Acme to confirm two things so we can put together a formal proposal: 
1) Confirm the economic buyer / budget owner (name/email) — is Tom Rivers the primary finance approver?
2) Confirm target unit economics: you gave a rough target of $X per 1M tokens in the call; can you give a target $/1M tokens (or a band) that would make this deal viable for Acme?

Ballpark from our side (subject to volume commit & contract term): $700–$1,200 per 1M tokens for hosted inference at the volumes you mentioned, or we can propose a Dedicated reserved pool with more aggressive unit economics (starting ~ $450–$800 per 1M tokens depending on commit and burst policy). I’ll let Aditya add more color on the unit economics and reserved options below.

I’ve attached a short pricing worksheet so you can drop in your expected monthly token volumes and see modeled cost. Next steps: once you confirm economic buyer + target $/1M, we’ll prepare a formal quote and a one-page mutual action plan (MAP) to get to PO/term sheet. Happy to set a follow-up with Tom + procurement next week if helpful.

Thanks,

--
Marissa Cole
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com
Redwood Inference

Attachments: Redwood-pricing-worksheet.xlsx (spreadsheet of modeled costs and options)

From: Maya Patel <maya@acme-ai.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Tom Rivers <tom.rivers@acme-ai.com>, procurement@acme-ai.com
Date: Tue, 10 Feb 2026 17:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intro + demo — pricing follow-up and next steps

Thanks Marissa — that recap looks right. A couple clarifications from our side: 

- Token volumes: the numbers you captured match our internal estimates (avg 3M/day, peak 10M/day, runway to 20–25M/day in 6–9 months). We’ll attach a brief usage export for last 30 days so you can validate the profile.
- Budget: Finance has earmarked roughly $75k/month as our preferred band for the next quarter, with upside if we see quality and reliability. Any proposal that meaningfully beats our current unit cost target will get expedited approval.
- Target $/1M: Finance asked us to propose something in the range of $500–$800 per 1M tokens for hosted inference — ideally closer to the $500 end if possible. If Dedicated/reserved gives lower unit cost, they’re open to exploring a committed contract.

Confirming: Tom Rivers (Tom.Rivers@acme-ai.com) is the budget owner and primary finance approver. Procurement is cc'd (procurement@acme-ai.com) and will handle contract routing.

Can you send a short formal quote showing both hosted (pay-as-you-go) and a 12-mo reserved commitment option with the unit economics for the volumes above? Attached: MAP-usage-report.csv (30-day token export).

—Maya
Maya Patel
Head of Product Operations | Acme AI
maya@acme-ai.com

Attachments: MAP-usage-report.csv (30-day token export)

From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya@acme-ai.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 11 Feb 2026 09:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Intro + demo — pricing follow-up and next steps

Thanks Maya — and thanks for the usage export. Quick sizing + unit-econ note from our side to make the hosted vs dedicated tradeoffs explicit: 

- Hosted (pay-as-you-go)
  - For the profile you shared (avg 3M/day, peaks ~10M/day): our standard hosted tier would land in the $700–$1,000 per 1M tokens band, with lower effective cost at sustained higher daily averages. Hosted keeps you on our multi-tenant runtime with fast onboarding and no infra ops.

- Dedicated (reserved 12-mo commit)
  - For a 12-month reserved pool sized for expected peak throughput, we can get unit economics in the $425–$650 per 1M tokens range depending on exact commit size, ingress/egress patterns, and whether you opt into aggressive quantization/optimizer bundles. Dedicated also gives you data isolation, higher SLA, and predictable throughput.

- Other levers we can use to hit the $500 target: longer term commit (24 months), commitment floors, or an initial pilot with staged discounts tied to day-30/day-90 usage thresholds. We can model a blended unit price across those levers.

If Tom is the budget owner, next step would be: Marissa will send a formal quote (hosted vs dedicated line items) + a one-page MAP. If Acme can indicate a target committed monthly spend (e.g., $75k/month), we’ll provide an option set that shows concrete unit price outcomes at that spend level.

Happy to jump on a short call with Tom + procurement to walk the numbers — Marissa, can you propose 30-min slots tomorrow or Thursday?

Thanks,
--
Aditya Rao
Head of Solution Architecture | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com

- Procurement will handle contract terms; timeline: if we get a quote by EOD Thursday, Finance can review over next week, and we could be in contract discussion the following week.

Tom — we’d like Redwood to provide an option for: (A) hosted pay-as-you-go at a modeled $/1M for the avg/peak profile, and (B) a 12-mo reserved commitment option sized to peak throughput with the associated unit price and monthly commit. Also please show the modeled monthly cost at our $75k/month target.

Let me know what time works for a 30-min walkthrough (tomorrow or Thursday).

—Maya
